findings.title: Cancelling a child releases the shared write lane before its owned effects retire
evidence: A write-enabled child owns semaphore permits as ordinary locals inside shared_child_lane while awaiting child work.

The child starts a registered blocking filesystem operation or owned subprocess that is still alive when cancellation or a task deadline occurs. Such production operations exist in fs.rs atomic_write_resolved_inner and atomic_create_resolved_checked_cancellable.

Background cancellation drops work in the biased select before cleanup.settle waits for those registered effects. A batch deadline also explicitly drops in_flight futures. Dropping the lane future releases both semaphore permits immediately.

A different foreground or background child can acquire the released write lane and concurrency slot while the first child effect is still live. This violates the documented shared lane and concurrency ceiling even though the first job correctly remains Cancelling.
findings.requested_fix: Retain permits until the exact child effect scope actually settles, including future-drop cancellation and deadlines. The owner proposed reusing a per-child AgentWorkScope plus AgentRunCleanupGuard holding permits and a parent-scope registration; this satisfies the traced lifetime requirement without a separate registry.
findings.required_regression: Hold an actual registered first-child blocking effect, cancel/drop the first lane future, queue a second child, assert neither write nor concurrency capacity becomes available until the held effect is released and joined; then assert second child enters.

residual_risks: No additional confirmed defect found in exact session/store/pool provenance, imported data, coherent snapshots, or permission/teardown paths reviewed. This is a bounded independent review, not a proof of absence.
